articles.title: How NAT traversal works
articles.read_scope: Complete substantive prose, examples, NAT taxonomy, advanced cases, ICE discussion, and final recap. Diagram captions and mathematical claims read; probability calculations and network behavior not independently reproduced.

practice.trigger: Peers must communicate across heterogeneous networks they cannot reconfigure.
practice.problem: Static topology assumptions block useful connectivity or confuse reachability with identity.
practice.mechanism: Start with a usable relay, discover and check candidate paths concurrently, upgrade to a measured better path, and retain authenticated end-to-end identity across endpoint changes.
practice.limits: Direct paths require compatible network behavior. Relay reachability, capacity, probing cost, and protocol interoperability remain explicit assumptions.
practice.counterexample: STUN reports an observed mapping, not universal reachability. IPv6 still encounters firewalls; a blocked relay removes the proposed fallback.
practice.verification: Proposed: test relayed startup, direct upgrade, destination-dependent NAT, blocked UDP, mapping loss, downgrade, and identity continuity with a finite probing budget.

existing_skill_targets: architecture: planning topology and connection lifecycle
microservice-operations: operational objectives, capacity and trust boundaries
articles.new_skill_recommendation: No separate NAT skill justified by this read; a conditional connectivity-design reference can fit architecture. A protocol implementation requires its actual interoperability specification.

articles.title: Designing Sentry's cross-region replication
articles.read_scope: Complete substantive prose and code/query examples: requirements, alternatives, outbox storage/delivery, consistency audit, rollout, transaction timeouts and replication loops. Company delivery count not reproduced.

practice.trigger: One authoritative mutation must eventually update selected regional copies.
practice.problem: Ordinary writes can omit replication intent; one tenant can dominate processing.
practice.mechanism: Persist intent in the authoritative transaction, centralize ordinary mutation paths, audit bypass writes, and independently process bounded ownership shards. Establish delivery baselines before depending on copies.
practice.limits: At-least-once delivery requires receiver semantics, authority and freshness rules. Coalescing fits replaceable state, not every business event.
practice.counterexample: A snapshot alone does not prevent an older request overwriting newer state. Cross-region handlers can generate replication loops; remote calls can outlive local transaction bounds.
practice.verification: Proposed: cover save, bulk update, delete and bypass paths; interrupt delivery, repeat requests, delay older state, isolate a busy shard, and check convergence/loop detection.

articles.new_skill_recommendation: No new outbox package recommended. Existing data and messaging references own this mechanism; research retained only in this lane.

articles.title: Removing risk from our multi-region design with simulations
articles.read_scope: Complete substantive prose and examples, including silo definitions, model annotations, ORM boundary errors, tests in current/future modes, CI cost, diagnostic confusion, and staging coverage gaps. Diagrams not independently measured.

practice.trigger: A proposed code/data boundary changes many existing paths before physical extraction.
practice.problem: A plausible ownership diagram can miss actual dependencies and lost constraints.
practice.mechanism: Make proposed ownership executable, incrementally reject forbidden crossings, and compare representative journeys in current and future modes before moving storage.
practice.limits: Enforcement affects only inspected/tested paths; framework patches can confuse diagnostics and double execution adds CI cost. Physical transport and database properties need separate checks.
practice.counterexample: Complete passing tests still missed boundary errors discovered in staging because branches were uncovered. Metadata annotations alone do not replace foreign keys or transactions.
practice.verification: Proposed: reject a seeded forbidden crossing, preserve a legal journey in both modes, inventory uncovered crossings, then exercise physical separation and replacement constraints.

articles.new_skill_recommendation: Existing extraction package is the correct home; no new skill. Implemented conditional boundary-rehearsal reference with explicit limits.

articles.title: State Machine Testing with Echidna
articles.read_scope: Complete substantive prose, Haskell/Solidity model and commands, initialization and transition defects, generated histories, shrinking and conclusion. Historical tool API and quoted run outputs not executed.

practice.trigger: An action result or legality depends on preceding operations.
practice.problem: Isolated examples miss an incorrect initial state or state transition.
practice.mechanism: Independently define states, initial state, actions, preconditions, transitions and invariants; execute generated histories against the implementation and retain reduced disagreements.
practice.limits: The model can share a specification mistake. Finite sequential histories do not prove concurrency, durability, all-input correctness, or current Echidna API compatibility.
practice.counterexample: The article has a prose sentence reversing locked/unlocked push outcomes; code and falsifying histories consistently show the intended rule. Generation restricted to legal actions leaves invalid-action rejection untested.
practice.verification: Proposed: seed wrong initialization or a missing transition, require the expected assertion to fail, then replay explicit reduced actions after resetting state.

existing_skill_targets: failure-oriented-testing: state-dependent histories and independent oracle
microservice-data: durable workflow states where cross-owner changes apply
articles.new_skill_recommendation: Existing testing reference is sufficient for testing. Designing a lifecycle remains an architecture/domain question, not a reason to duplicate this testing workflow.

articles.title: Tracing Discord's Elixir Systems (Without Melting Everything)
articles.read_scope: Complete substantive prose, code examples, envelope rollout, fanout sampling, independent profiling, overhead reductions and user-impact example. Charts and reported production numbers not independently reproduced.

practice.trigger: Cross-process observability must evolve while old and new message senders coexist.
practice.problem: Manual context handling hinders adoption; a sampled large fanout creates unbounded telemetry cost.
practice.mechanism: Normalize old/plain and new/enveloped messages at one interface, scope context to handling, and budget sampling by fanout while measuring instrumentation overhead independently.
practice.limits: Suppressing unsampled context changes continuity and can create fragment roots. Workload rates and CPU gains are company observations, not defaults.
practice.counterexample: The illustrated detach follows the handler call; a handler exception skips it unless cleanup is protected. A flat downstream sampling rate can erase small fanouts.
practice.verification: Proposed: exercise mixed sender versions, absent/malformed context, handler errors, small/large fanouts and no extra root generation; measure CPU, exported spans and correlation continuity.

existing_skill_targets: microservice-operations: cross-service observability and workload budgets
articles.new_skill_recommendation: Prefer conditional compatibility and observability references. A general operability skill would need a distinct activation/evidence contract beyond this existing operations package.
